content_voiceover: This is the Taiwan treatment algorithm for low to intermediate risk M D S, adapted from N C C N guidelines, and it starts after supportive care, iron folate and B twelve replacement, and C M V safe transfusions. The first branch point is cytogenetics. If there's a deletion of 5 q, lenalidomide is the go to agent. Without deletion 5 q, you look at ring sideroblast percentage. Under fifteen percent, or under five percent with an S F 3 B 1 mutation, you check serum erythropoietin. Low E P O favors an erythropoiesis stimulating agent, while high E P O routes you toward either immunosuppression with A T G and cyclosporine if there's good probability of responding, or hypomethylating agents like azacitidine or decitabine if the probability is poor. On the right side, ring sideroblasts fifteen percent or greater point you toward E S A plus G C S F or luspatercept depending on E P O level. The blue bar at the bottom is important for local practice, it marks each drug's Taiwan indication approval and reimbursement status as yes or no, since not everything on the N C C N pathway is actually reimbursed here.
keypoints: Del 5q positive drives lenalidomide as first line
No del 5q: branch by ring sideroblast percent and SF3B1 status
Serum EPO threshold of 500 guides ESA versus HMA or IST choice
Ring sideroblasts 15 percent or more favors ESA+GCSF or luspatercept
Red boxes show Taiwan-specific approval and reimbursement status
keypoint_voiceover: Remember this flow as a decision tree, first cytogenetics for del 5 q, then ring sideroblast burden, then serum E P O to pick between E S A, immunosuppression, or hypomethylating agents. And don't forget the Taiwan specific reimbursement flags, since board questions here often test what's actually approved locally, not just what's in the N C C N guideline.
